title: Why Criminals Love the Chinese Economy
gist: Alvin Camba (in an essay cut short by a paywall) argues China's economic rise has a darker, underexamined side: an outsize role in the global illicit economy, including buying roughly 90% of Iran's sanctioned oil (relabeled as Malaysian-origin) and hosting crypto brokers that help North Korean hackers launder funds — activity Beijing either cannot or will not crack down on.

themes.theme: China as hub for sanctions evasion and illicit finance

insights.claim: China purchases roughly 90 percent of Iran's sanctioned oil exports, which often arrive relabeled as originating from Malaysia and are paid for with money routed through small banks and shell companies acting as intermediaries.
insights.speaker: Alvin Camba
insights.so_what: Quantifies China as the dominant, near-monopoly buyer of sanctioned Iranian oil via a documented relabeling/shell-company laundering mechanism — a concrete data point for assessing sanctions efficacy and Iranian oil-revenue flows.
insights.quote: China purchases roughly 90 percent of Iran’s sanctioned oil exports, which often arrive relabeled as originating from Malaysia and are paid for with money routed through small banks and shell companies acting as intermediaries.

insights.claim: Cryptocurrency brokers based in China and Hong Kong help North Korean state-linked hackers launder stolen funds.
insights.speaker: Alvin Camba
insights.so_what: Identifies China/Hong Kong-based crypto brokers as a persistent laundering channel for North Korean cyber-theft proceeds, relevant to crypto-exchange compliance risk assessment and sanctions-evasion tracking.

insights.claim: Beyond its manufacturing and export dominance, China plays an outsize and underappreciated role in the illicit global economy — a 'darker side' of its economic rise that Beijing either cannot or will not crack down on.
insights.speaker: Alvin Camba
insights.so_what: Frames China's economic model itself as structurally entangled with sanctions-evasion and illicit-finance networks, a factor to weigh when assessing the durability of U.S./allied sanctions regimes against Iran and North Korea.
insights.quote: But there is another, darker side of China’s dominance: its outsize role in the illicit global economy.
